description: ECHO (Enforcement and Compliance History Online) is the EPA website for searching regulated facilities and their environmental compliance and enforcement records under the Clean Air Act, the Clean Water Act, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act for hazardous waste and the Safe Drinking Water Act. It offers facility searches by location, name or programme, an enforcement case search over civil cases in the Integrated Compliance Information System (ICIS) and criminal cases in the Summary of Criminal Prosecutions, dashboards, maps and trend charts, a Corporate Compliance Screener, ECHO Notify alerts, a Water Pollutant Loading Tool and the ECHO Clean Air Tracking Tool. It is run by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency with data from EPA and state agencies. Coverage is national. Data are available free online and as downloads, including the ECHO Exporter zip file of more than 1.5 million regulated facilities with Toxics Release Inventory releases, industry codes, permit types and coordinates, plus web and map services, all refreshed weekly. Caveats: records depend on what agencies enter in national systems, the Exporter is too large for Excel, and compliance status is not a measure of physical risk. For simulation it provides a geolocated inventory of industrial, chemical and utility facilities with their violation history for hazard exposure and resilience studies. It is related to the EPA Facility Registry Service record in this catalogue, whose FRS ID joins ECHO files to other datasets.
